sections.title: 十二、阅读文化习俗信息表判断正误
sections.passage:
When you travel to different countries, you may see people do things in different ways. Some bow (鞠躬) to say hello. Some kiss on the cheeks. These customs are really not the same in different cultures. Let's look at some examples.

- People bow to say hello and show thanks. (Japan)
- People kiss on both cheeks when they meet. (France)
- People take off their shoes before entering a house. (Japan, Korea, and many Asian countries)
- People eat with their right hand. The left hand is for other things. (India)
- People stand on the right side of the escalator(自动扶梯) and walk on the left. (The United Kingdom)

No custom is right or wrong. They are just different. When we travel, we can learn, respect, and even enjoy these differences. That's the real joy of seeing the world.

In the Philippines, some people ride jeepneys. These are colourful, long jeeps that were originally (最初地)made from old US army jeeps. In the desert areas of Egypt and Morocco, people still ride camels. Camels can go for days without water.

sections.title: 十四、阅读理解 B (La Tomatina)
sections.passage:
Have you heard of La Tomatina(番茄大战)? It is a fun festival in Buñol (布尼奥尔), a small town in Spain. It happens on the last Wednesday of August every year. During the festival, people throw tomatoes at each other. Thousands of people come from all over the world to join.

The festival began in 1945. During a local parade, some young people had a fight in the street and used tomatoes from a nearby vegetable stand (蔬菜摊). The next year, they brought their own tomatoes and had a tomato fight again. It became a tradition.

Before the fight, people put up a large greased pole (涂满油脂的木杆). They try to climb it to get a ham on top. When someone gets the ham, the tomato fight begins. Trucks bring over one hundred tons of tomatoes into the town. People throw tomatoes for about one hour. Then fire trucks spray (喷洒) water to clean the streets.

After the fight, everyone is covered in red. The town becomes very clean, because tomato acid helps wash away the mess and make the streets shine.

La Tomatina is a joyful celebration of fun and community.
